chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Karram, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have made it upon myself to fast until the Rising of the Qaim (peace be upon him).' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Fast, and do not fast during the journey, nor the two Eids, nor the days of Tashreeq, nor the day wherein there is doubt from the month of Ramadan.'

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What are the exemptions for continuous fasting vows in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a continuous vow (Kaffarah or Nadhr) does not override the established Sharia exemptions, reflecting the Shia principle that specific obligations yield to general dispensations. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that travel, Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, and the Days of Tashreeq (11th-13th of Dhu al-Hijjah) are valid breaks, ensuring the vow remains sustainable until the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (AJ). This ruling underscores the balance between devotional commitment and practical religious ease in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Karram who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I made it upon myself that I would be Fasting until the rising of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fast, and do not Fast during the journey, nor the two Eids, nor the days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> & 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja), nor the day wherein is a doubt from a Month of Ramazan’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Karram who has said the following: “Once, I said to abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I have placed upon myself to fast until the rise of al-Qa”im, (the one who rises with Divine Authority).
He (the Imam) said, ’Fast but do not fast on a journey, or the two ‘Id, the days of tashriq (11, 12 and 13) and the day which is doubtful about its being of the month of Ramadan.”’
